title: Delegates and events — remember
rememberThis: A delegate is a CLR type that holds a method group with a compatible signature, including return type.
Multicast invocation walks GetInvocationList() synchronously; one throw stops later handlers unless you iterate yourself.
event is not a public delegate field: outsiders may += and -= only, never assign or invoke.
Lambdas capture unless static; captured locals become a closure class and pin the enclosing object if you capture this.
C# 14 extension blocks add instance and static extension properties and operators; they still lose to real instance members at bind time.
bullets: Prefer Func<T,TResult> and Action<T> over custom delegates unless the name is part of a public event contract.
Long-lived SQS or RabbitMQ hosts that expose events must unsubscribe or use weak patterns; otherwise workers leak.
Local functions can yield and avoid a delegate allocation; lambdas cannot yield.
C# 14 lets lambda parameters take ref/in/out/scoped without spelling the types; params still needs types.

rows.label: Func vs Action
rows.value: Func returns TResult; Action returns void. Predicate<T> is Func<T,bool> with a name.

rows.label: Multicast +
rows.value: Combining two delegates builds a new invocation list. -= removes the last matching entry.

rows.label: static lambda
rows.value: Cannot capture locals, parameters, or instance state. Use it on hot paths to prove no closure.

rows.label: event vs delegate
rows.value: Public EventHandler is a field anyone can null out. event add/remove protect the list.

rows.label: C# 14 extension
rows.value: extension(T receiver) { ... } inside a static class; static extension(T) for type-level members.
